children: India has started the semiconductor manufacturing journey with a measured and calibrated programme, which was focused on getting the right talent, making sure that the ecosystem builds in our country, Ashwini Vaishnaw, Minister of Electronics and Information Technology, said here on Thursday.
Speaking at the inaugural session of the ‘Semicon India 2026’, he said that the Semicon 1.0 was the beginning with the foundation, and now the country has to build the building over this foundation.

“The Semicon 2.0 will build the semiconductor industry over six pillars. Number one is Design. In Semicon 1.0, we had lots of startups trying to begin, trying to see how we can design the chips. We had good success, more than 105 startups could participate in it, and about 20 of them got VC funding of about Rs.800 crore. But that was just the beginning. This time, our ambition is much bigger. We would be targeting at least 200 startups and companies which design chips in India across the spectrum of semiconductor requirements,” Vaishnaw said.

The pillar number 2 will be machines and materials, he said mentioning that more than 28 countries are participating in this event and whether it is capital equipment, maintenance facilities, chemicals, gases, every part of the ecosystem all are showcasing their expertise.
Pillar number 3 will be more display memory and fabs and Pillar number 4 will be more advanced packaging units.

“We already have a 3D packaging unit coming up in Odisha. We would like to have much progress in the advanced packaging, because that is a very important part of the entire value chain,” the minister said.

Pillar 5 will be research and development (R&D) and thus time, government will take up projects where some really cutting-edge industry required R&D can be taken up, he said adding that it would be fully driven by the industry and academia.

“It won’t be an isolated kind of R&D. It will be very applied kind of R&D that we would be looking at, and I’ll request the industry participants present here to suggest the projects that you would like to take up. We have very strong academia in our country, very strong base,” Vaishnaw said.

 “The pillar 6 is about talent. In the Semicon 1.0 we promised that we will train 85,000 design engineers over a period of 10 years. Happy to report that in just four years, we have been able to train around 70,000 design engineers, and in not just the big cities but throughout the country,” he noted.
Speaking at the session, Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said that the company plans to scale up chip assembly and testing facility here by multifold next year.
“This year, we will assemble and test tens of millions of chips at Sanand. Next year, hundreds of billions of chips,” he said.

Mehrotra said that Micron designs memory chips in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, assembles in Gujarat, and ships them to customers in every continent. He said Micron’s current production capacity already exceeds the memory required for India’s entire laptop market.

“Earlier this year, we began commercial production at Sanand, Gujarat. It is the first semiconductor assembly and test facility here in India and the first project under the finished DRAM and NAND products are now leaving Gujarat for customers around the world carrying a label this country has waited a long time to put on a memory chip - the Made in India,” he added.

Similarly, Infineon Technologies CEO Jochen Hanebeck said the country’s chip ecosystem is entering an exciting new chapter, underpinned by economic growth, deep industrial ambitions, and expanding technological capabilities.
He said Infineon has expanded its Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Ahmedabad, strengthened its R&D presence in Hyderabad, and is setting up a new state-of-the-art campus in Bengaluru.

“For Infineon, India is a market of tremendous importance. Today, we work with more than 1,200 customers across the country, ranging from startups to some of India’s largest and most successful companies,” Hanebeck added.

title: SEMICON India 2026: India’s semiconductor manufacturing journey a measured, calibrated programme: Vaishnaw
